title: Warp-prefetch slice heuristics for FlashAttention with paged KV
content:
Objective:
This note captures an exploratory design and a small set of heuristics for a warp-cooperative prefetch + slice scheduling strategy targeting FlashAttention-style fused attention kernels when used with a paged KV cache. The goal is to reduce tail latency for long-context chat workloads while keeping per-token cost bounded (i.e., avoid full KV warming), and expose simple knobs for runtime autoscaling/batching decisions.

Context / problem statement:
- Production workload: many short requests interleaved with occasional long-roll-forward chat sessions that read large KV histories.
- Serving runtime uses paged KV: KV entries are sharded into fixed-size slabs (pages) evicted to host/DRAM when GPU memory is constrained.
- FlashAttention fused kernels are high-throughput for dense attention but expect contiguous memory for Q/K/V. Paged KV causes non-contiguous accesses and spikes in demand to bring pages into GPU memory.
- We need kernel-level cooperation that: minimizes additional warp stalls due to page faults/prefetch, avoids saturating PCIe/NVLink with naive prefetching, keeps FlashAttention's fused path (block-systolic/shared-mem based) usable, and gives the runtime predictable signals for routing/fallbacks.

Design constraints and desiderata:
- Keep per-request overhead low: per-request state in the scheduler must be O(#pages accessed) not O(context_length * d_model).
- Avoid global synchronous page loads whenever possible. Prefer staggered, bandwidth-aware prefetches.
- Maintain compatibility with existing FlashAttention kernels (we cannot rewrite all kernels). Prefer a thin wrapper that can prefetch and then launch fused kernel on ready pages.
- Allow graceful degradation: if prefetch queue is saturated, fall back to a non-fused attention kernel that streams from global memory with lower memory residency pressure.
- Heuristics should be tunable by the runtime and derived from observed per-tenant latency percentiles.

High-level approach:
1) Slice the attention over sequence length into fixed "page-aligned slices". A slice maps to one or more KV pages (slabs). Each slice is processed by a group of cooperating warps (a cooperative block).
2) During request admission, the runtime computes the list of KV pages needed for the slices in priority order (most recent slices prioritized).
3) Prefetch scheduler issues small, bandwidth-shaped read requests for KV pages before launching the fused kernel for a slice. These reads populate GPU L2/L1 and/or allocate the resident page frames for the slice.
4) Warps executing the fused kernel poll a lightweight in-GPU-ready-bit cache (atomic flags) per page to decide whether to proceed with fused path or divert to streaming fallback.
5) Eviction hints are emitted: when a slice finishes, the kernel can attempt a soft hint to the KV manager (e.g., mark page as LRU candidate) to keep working set small.

Detailed kernel cooperative pattern:
- Thread block layout: one cooperative thread-block (CTB) handles a slice of S tokens. Within the CTB, warps are assigned bands of heads and token ranges for Q*K/V matmuls.
- Shared memory layout: store tile of Q and a compact page metadata (page_id, ready_bit) per slab. Avoid storing whole K/V tile in shared mem for paged cases; instead, use cooperative warp gather into registers + L2 prefetch.
- Prefetch path (two-stage):
  a) Controller (host or lightweight on-GPU tasklet) enqueues page fetch requests to an ordered per-request queue. Each request contains page_id, priority, desired_ready_ts.
  b) DMA worker issues pinned host->device transfers or NVLink fetches in small chunks (64KB-256KB) rather than full page when possible to spread bandwidth. The idea is streaming-in the frequently touched stripe first.
- Kernel arrival logic: when kernel starts for a slice it checks ready_bit for each page, if >= threshold (e.g., 70% of page stripes present), launch fused FlashAttention. If not, attempt a microfill: cooperative warps perform a direct gather from host memory with prefetch intrinsics (cudaMemcpyAsync to a staging buffer or direct loads if UVA), then run a slightly modified attention kernel that tolerates missing cache lines.

Bandwidth-aware prefetching heuristics:
- Limit outstanding inflight page fetches per-GPU to B_max = floor(total_nvlink_bandwidth / expected_page_bandwidth_per_fetch) * safety_factor. In practice we cap at 16-32 concurrent page downloads per GPU for mixed workloads.
- Throttle per-request prefetches when queue depth exceeds a soft-limit (Q_soft). Use exponential backoff per-request.
- Priority ordering: newest n slices > active qps slices > background eviction refill. Slices that will be executed within latency SLO window get high priority.

Prefetch granularity and tile sizing:
- Page size is a unit imposed by paged-KV: 1–4MB slabs depending on model. We propose to prefetch in smaller micro-stripes: 64KB–256KB stripes inside a page, aligned to typical L2/L1 cache line groups.
- Tile sizing for fused attention must aim to keep shared mem footprint < 32–48KB per CTB for Ampere/Blackwell GPUs. Choose S (tokens per slice) so that Q_tile + head_tiles + small K/V window fits in shared memory. Heuristic: S = clamp( (SMEM_budget - meta)/per_token_tile, 8, 64 ).

Mixed-precision and quantized KV considerations:
- If K/V pages are stored in quantized format (e.g., Q5/Q4), prefetch should bring the quantized bytes. Unpacking or fused dequantization can be performed inside the CTB before the matmul. Avoid host-side dequant to reduce PCIe bandwidth.
- For 8-bit or lower quantization, alignment matters: pack stripes to be friendly to coalesced loads. Add an unpack stage using warp-level intrinsics to expand into fp16 registers.
- Heuristic: if quantized page present but dequantization compute > 10% of attention kernel time, consider fetching a dequantized hot-strip from host if network cost is acceptable. (Runtime knob).

Ready-bit design and in-GPU coordination:
- Ready state per page is a small 32-bit word in device memory (or in a lightweight per-GPU status buffer). Bits: present_flag, stripes_present_count (8 bits), epoch/cookie (8 bits), reserved.
- Writers: DMA worker or host-overwrite sets flags atomically when stripe arrives. Readers: CTB checks flags with an atomic load + lightweight spin-wait (bounded spins) before fallback.
- Spin-wait policy: busy-spin for up to T_spin_us (e.g., 50–150us) then fallback to streaming path. This avoids long stalls while still benefiting short prefetch races.

Fallback streaming kernel:
- A fallback kernel is a version of attention that streams K/V from global memory in small chunks without requiring full residency. It uses smaller shared mem, more frequent sync points, and releases pages when done. It has lower throughput but predictable latency.
- Runtime decision: if page ready fraction < threshold at time of scheduling, immediately launch fallback kernel; otherwise attempt fused kernel.

Eviction and soft-hinting:
- When a slice completes, the CTB issues an async hint to the KV manager (via a device->host small ring buffer) with page_id and weight (how recently it was used). The KV manager uses these hints to bias LRU and to avoid prefetching pages that will be immediately evicted.
- Heuristic: track per-request reuse count for pages. If reuse_count < 2, deprioritize that page for future prefetches. This helps with ephemeral reads during rewind-heavy workloads.

Instrumentation and observability signals to expose:
- Per-slice metrics: pages_requested, pages_fulfilled, avg_prefetch_latency, fallback_count, fused_kernel_launch_time, streaming_kernel_time.
- GPU-side counters: DMA inflight count, total bandwidth consumed by prefetches, spin-wait time distribution. Surface these in per-model and per-route dashboards to tune knobs.

Microbench plan (experiments to run):
1) Baseline: FlashAttention fused kernel on fully warmed KV (control).
2) Naive: schedule fused kernel and let page faults trigger synchronous host transfers (worst-case).
3) Prefetch stripes with B_max limiter and test different stripe sizes (64KB/128KB/256KB) measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU bandwidth utilization.
4) Test spin-wait thresholds T_spin_us = {0, 50, 150, 500}us to find sweet spot for our network and NVLink latency profile.
5) Quantized pages: compare in-kernel dequant vs host-side dequant fetch for Q4/Q5 pages. Measure added kernel compute vs PCIe savings.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to safely measure page-level reuse_count without adding heavy per-request state? (approx: probabilistic counting via small bloom counters?)
- What interaction with GPU eviction policies (MIG/shared allocation) is expected in cloud GPUs with multiple tenants? Does our ready-bit need per-tenant isolation?
- Should we accelerate ready-bit checks with cudaMemPrefetchAsync for UVA systems vs explicit DMA? When does one approach dominate?
- Need to prototype a minimal DMA worker that can be scheduled by the runtime (or run as a persistent kernel) and measure overhead.

Action items:
- Prototype a microbench kernel that: (1) checks ready bits, (2) executes fused attention when ready, (3) falls back to streaming otherwise. Owner: Diego. Target: small repo branch + perf harness. (2 weeks)
- Implement a simple in-GPU ready-buffer ring and DMA simulator to test stripe sizes. Owner: Priya. (2 weeks)
- Add per-slice telemetry hooks in the runtime + dashboard spike. Owner: Ethan. (1 sprint)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: aim for a hybrid prefetch+fallback approach rather than a heavy rewrite. The heuristics should be conservative out of the gate (favor fallback over long spins).
- Real-world tuning will depend heavily on NVLink/PCIe bandwidth and model d_model. We'll likely need model-specific profiles to set stripe size and slice token counts.

References and background reading:
- FlashAttention paper and kernels (internal folder + external repo).
- Prior paged-KV docs in this repo: tag: paged-kv-arch.
- Slack thread: warp-prefetch-experiments (linked in artifacts).

Appendix: rough pseudo-workflow (host side)
1) Admission: compute slices + page list.
2) Enqueue page prefetches with priorities.
3) Launch persistent DMA worker (if not running) to issue stripe fetches capped by B_max.
4) Launch CTB for slice. CTB checks ready-bits; if OK -> fused kernel path; else -> fallback streaming path.
5) CTB emits completion hint to KV manager.

End of note. This is a working doc; expect to iterate after initial microbench results.
